trickyParts: The stale-caller refusal is keyed on `PluginRelaunchable && PluginContract != DaemonAPIVersion`, not on `PluginRelaunchFor`: persist clears the capability hash the moment a relaunch moves the claim to launching, so a post-relaunch predicate is unreachable; the pre-relaunch window (a live-state claim between the boot or its registration and the relaunch) is the one the sentence describes, and a launching/launch-uncertain claim never holds a hash, so it keeps the machine's own answer (`TestRunWaitsToRelaunchAnUnfinishedClaimUntilOrphanReconciliationSucceeds` seeds a hash into a launching claim, so it now seeds `PluginContract: api.DaemonAPIVersion` too).
`register` runs `staleRegistration` before `ensureEnrolled`: a stale registration's process is let go by its relaunch and must not be enrolled with the secrets broker.

A controller grant's redemption consults no controller record (found by the simplify pass): the operator-bearer grant `legion status` redeems is also `Controller: true`, and after migration 0042 every existing controllers row is at plugin_contract 0, so a redeem-time record check would have refused the operator's own `legion status` at the first boot. Mint-time refusal (`controllerSessionGrant`) is where the controller session's staleness is decided; grants die with a restart.

The install wrapper writes its whole block to stderr (the shim reads the child's stdout as the RPC frame stream) and passes the agent argv as positional parameters after `$0`, never quoted into the script; the plugins root and generation directory are literal absolute paths so `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` names them. In the stage 4a checkpoint the one process whose cmdline survives the execs is the shim's, so the `--extension` assertion reads the shim's cmdline.

`bun add` refuses the image's unpacked plugin copies under /opt/legion (their manifests name the monorepo's workspace packages), so stage 4b names the latest published pair (resolved by `npm view` at run time) rather than an in-image path; 4b never installs it (every 4b claim registers at the branch daemon's own contract).

The pod's embedded Postgres is SQL_ASCII, so `internal/ompsessions`' two UTF-8 refusal cases fail there for the environment (the package is untouched by this branch); the NATS-backed `internal/daemon`, `intake` and `workflow` tests need Docker and are CI's.
